prompt: Expand ${...} property placeholders the way Maven does, including properties that refer to other properties. Complete PomPropertyResolver, then run the tests.
explanation: One pass walks the text with indexOf("${"), copies the plain stretches and swaps in whatever the map holds for each key. Because a substituted value can itself contain a placeholder, resolve repeats passes until a pass produces an identical string -- the fixed point. An unknown key is copied through unchanged, which both preserves it and makes the next pass identical so the loop ends; the 10-pass cap is the separate safety net for a cycle like a=${b}, b=${a}, which never reaches a fixed point.
hints: Write a private helper that does exactly ONE pass over the text, then call it in a loop from resolve.
In the helper, use indexOf("${", i) and indexOf('}', start); a StringBuilder collects the pieces as you go.
Stop the loop as soon as a pass returns a string equal to the one you passed in -- and also stop after 10 passes so a cycle cannot hang.
